html:
Constantine V was Byzantine emperor from 741 to 775, the son of Leo III. He was an able soldier and the most determined enemy of holy images among the emperors.

Early in his reign he had to win back the throne from his brother-in-law Artabasdos, who seized Constantinople and held it until 743. He then used the civil war that brought down the Umayyads to raid the Arab frontier. In the Balkans he led about nine campaigns against the Bulgars, winning at Anchialos in 763, and settled Christians from the eastern frontier in Thrace.

In 754 he called the Council of Hieria, which condemned the making and honouring of icons. Monks who resisted were humiliated, exiled or killed, and monasteries were closed. The image supporters who later wrote the history of iconoclasm hated him. They called him Kopronymos, "dung-named", from a story that he soiled the font at his baptism. He died on campaign against the Bulgars in 775.
sum: Constantine V was Byzantine emperor from 741 to 775, the son of Leo III. He was an able soldier and the most determined enemy of holy images among the emperors.
